boundTrackObject.legalName: Petition and Order of Expunction of Dismissed Charges under G.S. 15A-146(a) and (a1)
boundTrackObject.publicName: Clear a North Carolina charge that was dismissed
boundTrackObject.mechanism: On petition, the court expunges the records of a charge dismissed by the State or by the court, for a single dismissal under subsection (a) and for multiple dismissals under subsection (a1). There is no prior-conviction bar and no prior-expunction bar; the 2017 legislation eliminated the prior-expunction bar. A judge may grant the petition without a hearing under subsection (a6). Any petition under this section must be on a form approved by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
exclusions: No case with a felony charge dismissed pursuant to a plea agreement is expunged under subsection (a).

Effective for dismissals on or after December 1, 2025, a court dismissal of a charge against a defendant found incapable to proceed is not eligible. AOC-CR-287 (Dec. 2025) reflects this and does not limit the exclusion by date, which leaves earlier dismissals unresolved.
Out-of-state and federal convictions and charges are outside this relief; it reaches North Carolina records only.

destination.detail: Statewide statute with county venue. The petition is filed with the clerk of superior court on the AOC-approved form. Excluding automatic expunctions under subsection (a4), the clerk notifies State and local agencies of the order as provided in G.S. 15A-150 and forwards a certified copy to the Division of Motor Vehicles for expunction of any civil revocation where the underlying criminal charge is also expunged.

rules.filing: File the AOC-approved form with the clerk of superior court in the county where the charge was brought. G.S. 15A-146(c) requires any petition under this section to be on a form approved by the Administrative Office of the Courts.
rules.fees: none for a true dismissal. $175 applies where the charge was dismissed pursuant to a deferred prosecution or conditional discharge agreement. Separately, the costs of expunging the records required under G.S. 15A-150 are not taxed against the petitioner.
rules.feeWaiver: Where the $175 fee under G.S. 15A-146(d) applies and the petitioner cannot pay it, the operative expunction indigency filing is AOC-G-106, Petition to Proceed as an Indigent (printed revision 11/24, two pages), which the Judicial Branch's expunction fee answer links directly; its fourth principal election is 'Petition To File Expunction Petition', with an affidavit, a legal-services certification and court-order blocks. AOC-CV-226, Civil Affidavit of Indigency (Rev. 4/23), is supplemental financial information that many counties use when the court asks for more; it is not the expunction fee-waiver filing, and its side-two oath concerns arbitration fees and is never rewritten or presented as an expunction assertion. Benefit receipt (SNAP, TANF, SSI) and legal-services representation are selections on G-106 that require actual participant support; absence of benefit receipt does not by itself foreclose the separate inability-to-pay selection. Recorded 2026-09-06 from the owner-relayed research; not counsel approval. (Before 2026-09-06 this rule read: 'Indigency waiver available where a fee applies, on AOC-CV-226, including for petitioners receiving SNAP, TANF or SSI or represented by a legal services organization.')

rules.service: none required by the AOC form for dismissals. A DNA expunction application under G.S. 15A-146(b1) is a separate matter and must be served on the district attorney not less than 20 days before the hearing.

researchParticipantText.text: Filing fee and inability to pay. An ordinary dismissal petition under this route has no filing fee. The $175 fee applies when the dismissal resulted from the specified deferred-prosecution or conditional-discharge process. If that fee applies and you cannot afford it, submit the Petition to Proceed as an Indigent with your expunction petition. Complete only truthful answers and sign its affidavit before an official authorized to administer the oath. The court decides your request. Provide additional financial information if the court requests it.

generationRequirements.question: What is the file number of the case you want expunged?
In which North Carolina county was the charge brought?
What was the charge, as it appears on the court record?
On what date was the charge dismissed?
Was the charge dismissed by the State or by the court?
Are you asking to expunge more than one dismissed charge?
Was the dismissal part of a deferred prosecution or a conditional discharge agreement?
Was any felony charge in the case dismissed as part of a plea agreement?
Was the charge dismissed by the court because you were found incapable to proceed?

Have you checked whether this case already cleared automatically? Cases where every charge was disposed favorably on or after December 1, 2021 clear by operation of law 180 to 210 days after final disposition.
Is your DNA record or profile in the State DNA Database as a result of this case?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because a DNA expunction application under G.S. 15A-146(b1) carries its own service and hearing requirements and routes to a separate matter.

generationRequirements.question: Do you also have a nonviolent felony committed before age 18, or a prostitution offense, that you may want expunged later?
generationRequirements.conditionDescription: Asked because an expunction under G.S. 15A-146 may bar later relief under G.S. 15A-145.4 and 15A-145.6, so the order of filing matters.
